assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Four separate @TableTest methods: discountForTripCount (ladder), discountForCategoryAndTripCount (eligibility), countSingleTicketsInWindow (rolling window), calculatesDiscountEndToEnd (integration)

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note. It does not follow the ladder.
assertions.evidence: Row 'Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips' with CHILD category and Discount 20 across {1, 5, 40} trip counts

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: Rows show tiers: {1,2,3,4}→0%, 5→5%, {6-9}→5%, 10→10%, etc., up to 40+→40%. All nine tiers present.

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: countSingleTicketsInWindow table rows: 'Exactly 30 days ago is still in window | [30/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 1' and '31 days ago has fallen out | [31/SINGLE/ZONE_1] | 0'

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: Rows use {1,2,3,4}, {6,7,8,9}, {11,12,13,14}, {36,37,38,39}, {41,45,100} as value sets, not individual boundary rows

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables. A price application table (if present) should test the arithmetic without re-enumerating tiers.
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount establishes the mapping once; discountForCategoryAndTripCount and calculatesDiscountEndToEnd call it, not re-enumerate tier boundaries
